content.thinking: I need to draft the root cause and executive summary while being careful not to overstate what's known—the incident duration is a lower bound since it was still unresolved when I stopped observing metrics, and I've escalated this with a draft PR. I should flag my key assumptions: that io-pay's 503s were external rather than caused by io-shop, that no deploy or flag records means no changes actually occurred, and that the incident likely persisted beyond my last data point.

assumptions: The service was still failing at the last minute of metrics available, so the duration and all impact figures are lower bounds, not measurements of the full outage.

io-pay's 503 responses are assumed to originate at the provider and not to have been induced by io-shop (e.g. rate-limiting, credential expiry, or a bad request shape); this was not confirmed with the provider.

'No deploys or config changes' is based on the change-event and feature-flag sources returning zero records; it assumes those sources are complete and were reporting correctly, and it does not cover changes made outside them.
The investigation only read io-shop's own metrics and logs; no data from io-pay or from the network path between them was available to confirm where the 503s were generated.
The response actions recorded here are from the automated responder only. Any concurrent human action, and whatever ultimately restored service, is not captured in this record.
The draft pull request is a proposed fix and was unreviewed and unmerged at the time of escalation; it is not known to have mitigated anything.
input.executive_summary: Starting at 17:58 UTC on 26 September 2026, the account page of the online shop stopped working for shoppers. The page needs card details from an outside payments company before it can be shown, and that company's service started rejecting those requests. With no way to show the page without them, almost every shopper who opened their account page got an error instead, and pages that did respond were very slow. An automated alert fired about six minutes after the problem began, and the automated responder investigated, ruling out any recent change to the shop itself as the cause. Because the failure lay with an outside supplier, there was nothing the shop's own automation could restart or roll back, so it made no changes, opened a draft code change proposing a more resilient way to handle the supplier being down, and escalated to human engineers. The service had still not recovered when the available data ends, so the outage lasted at least as long as the window covered here and the true duration and shopper impact are likely larger than reported.
input.root_cause: The account page in io-shop makes a synchronous, hard-dependency call to the third-party payment provider io-pay (api.io-pay.example) for card details while rendering. At 17:58:00Z io-pay began returning HTTP 503 on /v1/shoppers/{id}/card, and because the call has no timeout budget, fallback, or degraded-render path, every failed lookup failed the whole page — errors went to essentially all account-page traffic and latency rose sharply as requests waited on the failing upstream. No io-shop deploy, config change, or feature-flag change was found in the preceding day or week, so the trigger was external; the amplification (one upstream's failure becoming a total outage of the page) is io-shop's own design.
